title: Pare — Token-efficient MCP servers for dev tools (git, npm, Docker, test runners)
description: Suite of 9 open-source MCP servers wrapping common developer tools (git, npm, Docker, test runners, search) with structured, agent-optimized output. Returns typed JSON instead of raw CLI output. Claimed up to 95% fewer tokens vs. raw CLI output per command. Design philosophy: reduce unstructured noise in responses so less room for misinterpretation. MIT license, actively maintained as of March 2026. Tools included: git, npm, Docker, test runner(s), search. Each server returns structured JSON with typed fields rather than raw terminal output.

redundancy_check.notes: No match in registry or completed evaluations. Existing dev tool integrations use raw Bash tool output. The Cloudflare Code Mode pattern (token-efficient API representation) is conceptually related but applies to MCP server design patterns, not bundled dev tool MCPs. Requires COMPARISON evaluation: measure actual token savings vs. using Bash tool directly for git/npm/docker commands, assess setup overhead.

evaluation.reasoning: The 95% token reduction claim is directionally plausible (raw npm/docker output is very verbose) but needs measurement against actual Bash patterns used in this system. Capability expansion is low (40) because these servers don't add new actions — they reformatted existing ones. The 9-server suite introduces installation and configuration overhead. Score of 57 is in the middle of NEEDS_RESEARCH range. Would need both verified star count AND measured token savings vs Bash baseline to cross 70.
research_questions: What is the GitHub star count for Dave-London/Pare?
Can individual servers be installed selectively (e.g., just git and npm, skip Docker)?
Run benchmark: `git status` via Bash vs. Pare git server — actual token comparison on this workspace.
Run benchmark: `npm list` via Bash vs. Pare npm server — token comparison.
Are there known conflicts with existing Bash-based git workflows (e.g., hooks, gh CLI)?
Does Tool Search Tool adequately defer the 9-server context overhead when they're not needed?
evaluation.re_evaluation_trigger: When benchmark comparison (Bash vs Pare) is measured on actual workspace commands, or when star count confirms community validation.
